description: Get the profitability, cash-flow and leverage metrics of a US public company, plus two parameter-free reference points. No price-based multiple is published, so none is returned and you must never compute one; if the user needs a price, ask for it and label it user-supplied. This is NOT an opinion of intrinsic worth — for that, call `compute_dcf` with assumptions you state explicitly, and present the result as a scenario, never as "the" fair value. Returns per-period data combining computed ratios (gross_margin, operating_margin, net_margin, ROE, ROA, ROIC, debt_to_equity, FCF, FCF margin) and reference_points (graham_number, ncav_per_share) — two assumption-free values computed directly from filed fundamentals, with no discount rate or growth assumption baked in. Profitability/cash-flow/leverage fields come from fact.parquet (PIT-safe via accepted_at). reference_points come from ratio.parquet's `valuation` category, precomputed at each fiscal period end from SEC filings data. A share price is never a Valuein figure: for a multiple on a price the user gave you, use `compute_price_multiples`, and call the price user-supplied with its date. Each value is a `{value, unit}` pair (unit varies: x / USD / percent); a null value carries a `null_reasons[field]` code — ALWAYS check it before assuming zero (null != 0). Use this *instead of* `get_financial_ratios` when the reference points matter; use `get_financial_ratios` when you only need the raw ratio table; use `compute_dcf` whenever the user is asking what the company is WORTH. Available on all plans.

as_of_date.description: Point-in-time date (YYYY-MM-DD). Only returns data with accepted_at on or before this date. Eliminates look-ahead bias for backtesting.

fiscal_year.description: Fiscal year (YYYY). Omit to return most recent periods.

limit.description: Maximum number of periods to return (1–40). Defaults to 5.

period.description: Filing period granularity. Annual uses 10-K; quarterly uses 10-Q.

ticker.description: Stock ticker symbol, e.g. AAPL, MSFT — or a CIK (SEC identifier), e.g. '0000320193'.

name: get_valuation_metrics

_meta.description: Response metadata (provenance, point-in-time flag, freshness, request id and warnings). Every field is documented once in the agent contract (agent_contract.meta in the server's manifest.json).

additionalProperties.description: Explicit availability status. A real reported zero is 'available' with value 0 — never null. 'not_reported' = filing omitted it; 'not_mapped' = XBRL mapping uncertain; 'suppressed' = below confidence; 'error' = compute/retrieval failed.

metrics_display.description: The figure rendered exactly as it should be quoted in prose ($402.83B, 59.65%, $6.11). QUOTE THESE VERBATIM. Do not re-render the raw number in `metrics` yourself: a figure you reformat no longer matches the string Valuein can bind to its filing, so it is reported to the reader as unverified even though the underlying fact was sound.

additionalProperties.description: Provenance pointer: origin 'dataset' carries the SHA-256 fact_id + source filing; origin 'computed' carries the formula + the input fact_ids (verify with verify_fact_lineage).

concept.description: Standard concept of the reported fallback fact that supplied the value, present only when it is not the metric's primary concept (e.g. NetIncomeToCommon, OperatingCashFlowContinuing)

derived.description: The receipt behind derived_id: the registered formula, the rendered figure, and the input facts.

derived_id.description: Citation id of a figure the server computed (drv1:...). Cite it exactly like a fact_id; verify_facts re-derives it from its input facts. Absent when no input fact could be resolved.

method.description: Set only on a discrete quarter the filer did not print itself: 'ytd_subtraction' (period-to-date minus the prior period-to-date) or 'q4_from_quarters' (fiscal year minus Q1-Q3). The figure is derived, not reported.

graham_number.description: sqrt(22.5 * diluted EPS * book value per share). A parameter-free screening threshold, NOT an intrinsic-value estimate — it takes no assumptions about growth or discount rate.

ncav_per_share.description: Graham net current asset value per share ((current assets − total liabilities) / diluted shares). A parameter-free liquidation-floor reference point, NOT an intrinsic-value estimate.

title: Valuation Metrics
